issue: getOrders (GET /api/orders, admin) returns ALL orders with no pagination and populates user on every row
estimated_impact: Linear growth in payload + DB work. At 10k orders: ~5-10MB JSON, 200-500ms query + serialise, event-loop block during JSON.stringify. p95 latency unbounded.
recommendation: Add pageSize/pageNumber like getProducts. Use .lean() to skip Mongoose hydration. Sort by createdAt desc + index.

issue: getMyOrders returns all orders for a user with no limit/pagination and no projection
evidence: const orders = await Order.find({ user: req.user._id })
estimated_impact: Power-users with many orders cause full-table scan + large payload. With 1k orders/user: ~500KB payload, missing index on user means full-collection scan = 100-500ms.
recommendation: Add pagination, .lean(), and ensure index on { user: 1, createdAt: -1 }. Project only fields needed by the orders list UI.

issue: getUsers (admin) returns all users in DB with full document (including password hash field via mongoose) and no pagination
estimated_impact: At 100k users: ~50MB payload, several seconds of JSON.stringify blocking the event loop. Also leaks password hash if Mongoose schema does not project it out.
recommendation: Add pagination + .select('-password') + .lean(). Add a search/filter param.

issue: getProducts uses countDocuments + find with $regex on name on every list request; no index on name and regex with leading-wildcard cannot use index anyway
evidence: const count = await Product.countDocuments({ ...keyword }); const products = await Product.find({ ...keyword }).limit(pageSize).skip(pageSize * (page - 1))
estimated_impact: Two sequential queries per request. countDocuments without index = collection scan on every search; at 100k products ~200-800ms each. Sequential awaits double the latency.
recommendation: Run countDocuments + find in Promise.all. Add text index on name (or use $text). Cap keyword length. Consider estimatedDocumentCount() when no filter.

issue: getPendingReviews scans every product to find embedded reviews with status='pending'; no index on reviews.status
estimated_impact: Full collection scan at 100k products. Returns ALL reviews (not just pending) and filters in JS — multiplies payload size by 10-100x. ~1-3s at scale, plus event-loop block while filtering.
recommendation: Use aggregation with $unwind+$match to return only pending reviews. Add multikey index on { 'reviews.status': 1 }. Also paginate.

issue: getTopProducts and getProductRecommendations sort by rating without a supporting index
evidence: Product.find({}).sort({ rating: -1 }).limit(3) and Product.find({ _id: { $ne: req.params.id } }).sort({ rating: -1 }).limit(3)
estimated_impact: Without index on rating, every call does a full sort. At 100k products, ~100-300ms; called on every home page / product page load.
recommendation: Add index on { rating: -1 }. Cache the result for ~60s — it changes only when reviews are moderated.

issue: MCP feature-flag tools use readFileSync/writeFileSync on every tool invocation (HTTP mode handles concurrent sessions)
estimated_impact: Event-loop block per tool call: at 319 lines (~10KB) features.json today the block is ~1ms, but as the file grows or the disk is slow (network FS, EBS) latency spikes. Blocks all concurrent MCP sessions. write fsync also blocks.
recommendation: Use fs/promises readFile/writeFile (await) as backend/routes/featureFlagRoutes.js already does. Also cache in-memory and invalidate on write.

issue: readFeatures() re-parses features.json on every MCP tool call — no in-memory cache like backend/utils/featureFlag.js has
estimated_impact: Hot path for the LLM agent that lists/inspects flags many times in a workflow. ~1ms per read at current size; scales linearly with file size. Redundant I/O and parse work.
recommendation: Cache parsed JSON in-process with 5s TTL (mirror backend util) or invalidate on writeFeatures().

issue: PATCH /api/featureflags/:key has a read-modify-write race; concurrent admin edits or backend+MCP simultaneous writes lose updates (also flagged in security-review SEC-16)
evidence: const data = await readFlags(res); ... data[key].status = status; ... await writeFile(tmp, ...); await rename(tmp, filePath)
estimated_impact: Functional correctness issue under concurrency; not a latency hit per se but causes silent data loss that is then debugged as a perf/consistency mystery.
recommendation: Serialise writes with an in-process mutex (async-mutex) or move to a real datastore. See security-findings.jsonl SEC-16.

issue: addOrderItems trusts client-side itemsPrice/totalPrice — when fixed (per security SEC-10) the natural implementation will fetch every product in a loop
evidence: const order = new Order({ orderItems, ..., itemsPrice, ..., totalPrice })
estimated_impact: Potential future N+1 of size = orderItems.length. With a 20-item cart and 5ms/query that's +100ms on the order-create path.
recommendation: When implementing server-side price recompute, use Product.find({ _id: { $in: orderItems.map(i => i.product) } }) — single query, not N.

issue: getProductById converts entire product to plain object then filters reviews in JS instead of projecting at the DB
evidence: const productData = product.toObject(); productData.reviews = productData.reviews.filter(r => r.status === 'approved')
estimated_impact: Per request: O(reviews) work plus full doc hydration. For a product with 1000 reviews (10% pending) you ship the pending ones to the server only to discard. ~1-5ms per call but inflates DB payload 1.1x.
recommendation: Use $elemMatch / aggregation to return only approved reviews, or store an approved-only denormalised array. Add .lean().

issue: createProductReview and moderateReview recompute rating average by iterating the full reviews array on every write
evidence: const approvedReviews = product.reviews.filter(r => r.status === 'approved'); product.rating = approvedReviews.reduce(...) / approvedReviews.length
estimated_impact: O(reviews) per write; for products with thousands of reviews this is noticeable on the write path. Also writes the full product doc back, not just the new review.
recommendation: Maintain running sum (ratingSum) + count in the schema and update incrementally. Use $push + $inc rather than .save() on full doc.

issue: User-controlled keyword passed to MongoDB $regex without escaping or length cap — both a ReDoS surface for the DB engine and a CPU pin (overlaps with security-findings SEC-9)
estimated_impact: Crafted patterns like '(a+)+$' or long alternations can stall the MongoDB regex engine. Even benign leading-wildcard regex blocks index usage → full collection scan per request.
recommendation: Escape metacharacters (already done in suggestProducts line 202), cap length to 100 chars, anchor with ^ where possible to use index prefix. Cross-ref security SEC-9.

issue: proshop-docs-index resource builds an unbounded Map by scrolling the entire Qdrant collection — fine today, but grows with project-data/
evidence: do { const response = await qdrant.scroll(COLLECTION, { limit: 100, offset, ... }); for (const point of response.points) { if (!seen.has(source_file)) seen.set(source_file, ...) } offset = response.next_page_offset } while (offset != null)
estimated_impact: Memory grows O(distinct source_files). At 10k docs, ~1MB heap per resource read. Each call also makes 100s of round-trips to Qdrant (limit=100). At current ~50 files this is trivial; flagging as it scales.
recommendation: Increase scroll limit (1000), or push the dedup into Qdrant via payload-index + facet query. Cache the index for the process lifetime — it changes only on re-ingest.

issue: ingest.js loads all chunks into memory before embedding+upserting; for a large project-data/ this is unbounded
evidence: const chunks = buildChunks() // loads all files; then iterates in batches of 96
estimated_impact: Peak heap = sum of all chunk text. At 1000 files × 5 chunks × 2KB = ~10MB today. Could grow to hundreds of MB if project-data/ becomes the actual prod docs corpus. Also if Cohere throttles, all chunks stay resident.
recommendation: Stream files: walkMd as a generator, accumulate one batch (96 chunks) at a time, embed+upsert, then drop. Caps memory regardless of corpus size.

issue: Embed batches are processed strictly sequentially; Cohere + Qdrant calls could overlap with bounded parallelism
evidence: for (let i = 0; i < chunks.length; i += BATCH_SIZE) { ... await cohere.embed(...); await qdrant.upsert(...) }
estimated_impact: Wall-clock for full ingest scales linearly with batches. At 50 batches × (200ms embed + 100ms upsert) = ~15s. With parallelism 3-4: ~5s. Run rarely so impact small; flag as low.
recommendation: Use p-limit to run 3-4 batches in parallel. Or pipeline: embed batch N+1 while upserting batch N.

issue: search_project_docs re-embeds the query through Cohere on every call; identical queries (very common during a single agent run) pay the full API roundtrip
evidence: embedResponse = await cohere.embed({ texts: [query], model: 'embed-multilingual-v3.0', inputType: 'search_query', ... })
estimated_impact: Cohere embed ~150-400ms per call + API cost. A workflow that searches the same phrase 5x pays 5x.
recommendation: Add an in-memory LRU (e.g., size 200) keyed by sha1(query) → vector. TTL ~10min is fine. Also makes the tool resilient to brief Cohere outages.

issue: Collection existence check (qdrant.getCollection) runs on every tool call before the search, adding a sequential round-trip
evidence: try { await qdrant.getCollection(COLLECTION) } catch { collectionExists = false } ... await qdrant.search(COLLECTION, { ... })
estimated_impact: Extra ~5-20ms per search. Mostly a problem for high-frequency callers.
recommendation: Check once at startup (main() already does this) and cache the result. On search, just let qdrant.search throw and convert the error.

issue: Every authenticated request performs a User.findById to populate req.user — no caching
estimated_impact: Each protected request = 1 extra round-trip DB query, ~2-10ms p50. On hot paths (e.g. /api/orders/myorders) this is unavoidable for freshness but compounds at scale.
recommendation: Optional: short-lived in-process LRU (30s TTL) keyed by user id. Or put isAdmin in JWT claim and only re-fetch on profile updates. Trade-off: stale isAdmin after demotion (already a security concern in SEC-3/SEC-5).

issue: getProducts is paginated; getMyOrders, getOrders, getUsers, getPendingReviews are NOT — all listed above

note: No loop-with-DB-call N+1 found in current controllers. Risk noted for future addOrderItems fix.
